newsitem.title: USA: Alcatel sees strong copper rod and wire growth.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel sees strong copper rod and wire growth.

text.p: The copper wire and cable market, the red metal's biggest consumer sector, is expected to grow 3 to 4 percent this year in North America representing an extra 75,000 tonnes of cathode, John Anderson, vice president and general manager, rod mill operations at Alcatel Cable in Canada told an industry gathering.
Rod and wire sectors consume some 2 million tonnes of copper in Canada and the United States annually, or 70 percent of total copper offtake in the region, Anderson estimated.

The demand for building wire, the biggest sector accounting for 33 percent of all copper consumed in wire and rod, was set to grow 0 to 1 percent this year as housing starts in the U.S. remain flat, though other construction such as commerial buildings will be stronger.
Growth in the magnet wire market will be 2 to 3 percent this year.
"Perhaps the most interesting sector is telephone cable. Left for dead by fibre optics a few years ago, copper telephone cable is expected to grow by at least 5 percent in 1997," Anderson said.
Fax modems, internet connections and home offices has boosted the use of copper in telephone wires to homes.

The fastest growth area for copper in the wire and cable sector in recent years has been the data cable area, Anderson said. In 1997, data cable growth is expected to moderate to 15 to 20 percent, down from almost 30 percent a year ago.
Threats to the wire and cable sector included imports, an economic downturn and substitution. "In general I believe we can fight off these threats," Anderson said.
